seo.title: Ventana Big Sur: Adults-Only Coast Honeymoon Review
seo.description: Adults-only Alila resort on Big Sur cliffs. Score 89/100, from $1,200/night. Verdict, suite pick, 7-night plan.

content.verdict: Ventana Big Sur is the second great cliff-edge adults-only resort on the Big Sur coast — a 59-room Alila by Hyatt property on 160 acres immediately south of Post Ranch Inn, sharing the same headland and effectively the same view, with a more contemporary architectural language and roughly two-thirds the per-night price. Opened in 1975 and substantially rebuilt in 2017 when Alila took over, Ventana now operates as adults-only (minimum age 18), all-inclusive (rates include breakfast, lunch, and unlimited wine and beer through the day — a genuine differentiator), and with a more relaxed atmosphere than the highly choreographed Post Ranch. Rooms are distributed across the cliff in clusters connected by wooded paths — the highest-grade Vista Suites have ocean views, private decks, fireplaces, and freestanding baths; the Glampsites (luxury safari-style canvas tents on platforms in the redwood grove) are an unusual and genuinely fun honeymoon option for one or two nights of the trip; and the Sur House restaurant has terrace dining with the Pacific in front. Two pools (one heated upper, one Japanese soaking bath), the Spa Alila (six treatment rooms, signature redwood-essence massage), and walking trails through the property to the cliff-edge meditation deck and the sunset terrace round out the proposition. The honeymoon move at Ventana is the Vista Suite for 3 nights, with one Glampsite night for variety, with daily yoga and a Sierra Mar non-resident dinner reservation at Post Ranch one evening for the special-occasion moment. Caveats: Ventana is not Post Ranch — the architecture is good rather than transcendent, the cliff-edge moments are slightly less dramatic, and the dining at Sur House is good rather than world-class. But for 70% of the experience at 60% of the price with all-inclusive food and drink — Ventana is the smart honeymoon move.
content.best_room: A Vista Suite (premier ocean-view room with private deck, fireplace, freestanding bath) is the honeymoon room. For variety, swap one night for a luxury Glampsite in the redwood grove. Avoid the Garden Suites without ocean view — the view is the differentiator.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Arrival and Sur House dinner
itinerary_7_nights.description: Fly Monterey (MRY) — 1h drive south. Check-in to your Vista Suite, welcome champagne. Dinner at Sur House on the terrace.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Big Sur drive south
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive Highway 1 south — Bixby Bridge, Pfeiffer Beach, McWay Falls. Lunch at Nepenthe. Return for sunset at the upper pool.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Spa day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Morning yoga at the cliff-edge deck. Long midday at the Spa Alila — couples’ redwood-essence massage. Lunch on your deck. Evening Japanese soaking bath under the redwoods.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Sierra Mar special-occasion night
itinerary_7_nights.description: Move into a Glampsite for one night in the redwood grove. Dinner at Sierra Mar next door at Post Ranch (book 60 days ahead — non-resident dinner reservations are rare but possible). Return for stargazing.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Carmel-by-the-Sea day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive 30 min north to Carmel — beach walk, gallery browsing, lunch at La Bicyclette. Return for the evening.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow cliff day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Morning at the upper pool, lunch on the deck, afternoon redwood walks. Final dinner at Sur House with paired wines.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow departure
itinerary_7_nights.description: Final breakfast on the deck, drive 1h to Monterey airport.

caveats: Highway 1 closure risk from mudslides — check Caltrans before flying.
Sur House dining is good but not Sierra Mar level — for the special-occasion night, book a non-resident reservation at Post Ranch’s Sierra Mar.

faqs.question: Good for honeymooners?
faqs.answer: Yes — the second-best honeymoon hotel on Big Sur after Post Ranch, with a more relaxed atmosphere and all-inclusive value. The Vista Suite plus one Glampsite night is the honeymoon move.

faqs.question: Best time to visit?
faqs.answer: April, May, September, October — best fog burn-off and warmest weather. June–August has more coastal fog. December has storm drama and the Keyhole Rock alignment.

faqs.question: Book in advance?
faqs.answer: Vista Suites for peak months: 6–9 months ahead. Glampsites: 4–6 months. Sierra Mar non-resident dinner reservation at Post Ranch: 60 days ahead through Post Ranch concierge.

faqs.question: Best room type?
faqs.answer: Vista Suite with ocean view, fireplace, deck. Try one Glampsite night for variety. Skip Garden Suites without view.

faqs.question: How to get there?
faqs.answer: Monterey (MRY) is 1h drive south on Highway 1. SFO 2h 45min. SJC 1h 45min. Hotel arranges transfer.
